verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's Wally CLI documents a one-command integration that points a tool at a model and starts it. The opencode coding agent can use a `--cloud` flag to target RunAnywhere's hosted models instead of local ones, and the hosted endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so agents built on OpenAI clients can use it as a backend. missing for 10: an enumerated list of supported coding agents beyond opencode, step-by-step per-agent setup docs, and independent hands-on corroboration of a coding agent running against it.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: One command points a tool at a model and starts it. There is nothing to configure by hand
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
The endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so the official OpenAI clients work by pointing `base_url` at it.
you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
